look_here_first: FIND THE TUMBLEWEED-LIKE, OPEN BROOM PANICLE rather than a crabgrass fingerhead. Many extremely fine wiry branches spread broadly, each carrying a small usually FUZZY oval spikelet; the branch axils are often swollen and surrounded by long white hairs. On a leaf, one edge can look pale and strongly crinkled or BACON-WAVY. This native-to-Texas perennial was formerly called Leptoloma cognatum; keep one species card.

best_field_traits: Perennial warm-season grass, with several slender, wiry often knotty stems emerging from a relatively horizontal, typically hairy basal crown.
Strongly open branched broomlike panicle, commonly up to about 30 cm long, widening substantially with maturity; mature panicle may detach and tumble.
Individual spikelets rather than tight rows along fingerlike branches; spikelets small, fuzzy/hairy, usually under about 3.3 mm.
Panicle branch nodes/axils often expanded or swollen and may show long radiating white hairs, useful as a high-value photo target.
Short relatively stiff flat blades often have a conspicuous pale, crinkled or wavy margin (one side can resemble a wavy saw). Do not call the species from this alone.
Plant color can shift pale green to straw/gold by fall; color alone is not diagnostic.
Formerly frequently treated as Leptoloma cognatum; ITIS and POWO accept Digitaria cognata, and this is not a second separate grass card.
crew_field_check: Photograph whole plant, stem/roots, whole seedhead and single spikelet from same mature individual.
Use panicle architecture FIRST; confirm true ligule and spikelet anatomy only with proper scale.
Never annotate a structural feature that is not physically resolvable in the source photo.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole perennial plant and basal crown in surrounding habitat, including leaves and flowering culms.
Entire detached-or-attached open broomlike panicle from side with ruler.
Macro of swollen branch axil with radiating long hairs; arrow only if actually visible.
One leaf edge spread flat showing pale crimped/corrugated margin and midvein.
One fuzzy ripe terminal spikelet at ≥10× with 1-mm reference.
Late-season panicle detachment/tumbling habit, only if observed on same species.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Southern crabgrass (D. ciliaris) has crowded fingerlike one-sided racemes carrying paired spikelets and is typically an annual spreading along the ground; D. cognata has a big widely branching diffuse panicle with tiny individual fuzzy spikelets and hairy swollen branch junctions. Some Panicum and Sporobolus have airy heads; check the distinctive wavy whitish leaf margin, pubescent swollen panicle branch axils and actual two-flowered spikelet anatomy. Three-awns (Aristida) produce conspicuous true floret awns; D. cognata spikelets are essentially awnless.
